t.13.1: Arjuna said: Prakṛti and Puruṣa, the field and the knower of the field, knowledge and that which is to be known, these I wish to learn, O Keśava.
t.13.2: The Blessed Lord said: This body, O Kaunteya, is called the field; the one who knows it is called the knower of the field by those who know of these things.
t.13.3: And know Me also as the knower of the field in all fields, O Bhārata. The knowledge of the field and the knower of the field, that is knowledge in My view.
t.13.4: Hear from me in brief what that field is, of what nature it is, what its modifications are, and from what it arises; and who he is and what his powers are.
t.13.5: It has been sung by the seers in many ways, distinctly in various hymns, and also in the words of the Brahmasūtras, well reasoned and conclusive.
t.13.6: The great elements, the ego-sense, the intellect and the unmanifest too, the ten senses and the one, and the five objects of the senses.
t.13.8: Absence of pride, absence of hypocrisy, non-violence, patience, uprightness, service of the teacher, purity, steadfastness, and self-restraint.
t.13.7: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, the aggregate, consciousness and steadfastness: this, in brief, is declared to be the field together with its modifications.
t.13.9: Dispassion toward the objects of the senses, and also absence of egoism; constant perception of the evil and suffering in birth, death, old age, and disease.
t.13.10: Non-attachment, freedom from clinging to son, wife, home and the like, and constant evenness of mind amid the arrival of the desired and the undesired.
t.13.11: Unswerving devotion to me through the discipline of exclusive union, resort to solitary places, and distaste for the crowds of men.
t.13.12: Constancy in the knowledge of the Self and insight into the purpose of the knowledge of truth: this is declared to be knowledge, and whatever is contrary to it is ignorance.
t.13.13: I shall declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality: the beginningless supreme Brahman, which is said to be neither being nor non-being.
t.13.14: With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads and mouths on every side, hearing everywhere, That abides in the world, enveloping all.
t.13.15: It shines through the qualities of all the senses, yet is devoid of all the senses; unattached, it nonetheless sustains all; free of the guṇas, it is yet the enjoyer of the guṇas.
t.13.16: It is outside and inside all beings, both unmoving and moving. Because of its subtlety it cannot be known; it is far away, and yet it is near.
t.13.17: Undivided, yet it abides among beings as if divided; that which is to be known is the sustainer of beings, their devourer, and their creator.
t.13.19: Thus the field, as well as knowledge and that which is to be known, have been briefly described. My devotee, having understood this, attains to My state of being.
t.13.18: It is knowledge, the object of knowledge, and that which is to be reached through knowledge; it is seated in the heart of all.
t.13.20: Know that prakṛti and puruṣa are both without beginning, and know also that the modifications and the guṇas are born of prakṛti.
t.13.21: Prakṛti is said to be the cause in the agency of effect and instrument; Puruṣa is said to be the cause in the experiencing of pleasures and pains.
t.13.22: For the puruṣa, abiding in prakṛti, experiences the guṇas born of prakṛti; attachment to the guṇas is the cause of its births in good and evil wombs.
t.13.23: The supreme Puruṣa in this body is the witness and the one who consents, the sustainer, the enjoyer, the great Lord, and is also called the Supreme Self.
t.13.24: He who thus knows the Puruṣa and Prakṛti together with the guṇas, though he may be living in any way whatsoever, is not born again.
t.13.25: Some, through meditation, behold the Self in the self by the self; others by the yoga of Sāṃkhya, and still others by the yoga of action.
t.13.27: Whatever being comes into existence, whether unmoving or moving, know that it arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field, O bull among the Bharatas.
t.13.26: But others, not knowing in this way, worship after hearing from others; and they too, devoted to what they have heard, surely pass beyond death.
t.13.28: He who sees the Supreme Lord abiding equally in all beings, the imperishable within the perishing, truly sees.
t.13.29: For seeing the Lord as equally present everywhere, he does not harm the self by the self; thereupon he goes to the supreme goal.
t.13.30: He who sees that all actions are performed in every way by Prakṛti alone, and likewise sees the Self as the non-doer, he truly sees.
t.13.31: When he sees the separate existence of beings as resting in the One, and their expansion from that alone, then he attains Brahman.
t.13.32: Because it is without beginning and without qualities, this imperishable Supreme Self, though dwelling in the body, O Kaunteya, neither acts nor is tainted.
t.13.33: Just as the all-pervading ether, because of its subtlety, is not tainted, so the Self, though present everywhere in the body, is not tainted.
t.13.34: Just as the one sun illumines this entire world, so does the lord of the field illumine the entire field, O Bhārata.
t.13.35: Those who, with the eye of knowledge, thus know the difference between the field and the knower of the field, and the liberation of beings from Prakṛti, go to the Supreme.
